decision: Organisation size at go-live with live money: F3 (founder, CTO, controller, plus contracted reviewer and approvers) vs F5 (five core) vs F6+
working_claim: A 3-person core is the minimum safe organisation at go-live (research headline).
admissibility: Fails: unbounded ('minimum safe' without the conditions CNV-GOV-003 sets) and false precision (break-even differences of $0.03-0.06B between F3 and F5 come from [A] parameters). Restated: 'Before auditor/board acceptance of the deterministic gate, F3 can release payments only with a sponsor-appointed third person, and release stops when either internal authority is absent.'
mechanism: Payment release needs separation (preparer, approver, releaser) and absence cover; December demand runs 2-3x the monthly average; reconciliation must be outside the payment chain.
signal: Entry signal: the auditor's SoD acceptance letter or the sponsor appointee roster.
incentives: Founders gain from a low burn. The sponsor bears the third-person and suspended-release cost. Contractors bill hours; they carry no tenure, so they have little incentive to hold control knowledge.
bounds: Holds below ~3,000-5,000 accounts and outside December; fails under double absence (CNV-GOV-004 test).
tradeoffs: F3 saves ~$0.25-0.4M/yr vs F5 in payroll but buys ~4 contracted FTE at $1.45B (E05) and transfers release risk to sponsors.
operational_test: Fails under pressure: December plus one absence leaves F3 with one internal authority, so release suspends (Design.fs controlCheck note).
correctability: Low correctability (a control failure on charitable money damages trust in a way hiring cannot quickly repair)
constraints: CNV-GOV-003 (three distinct persons until accepted); CNV-GOV-004 (sponsor-appointed reserved authority, exclusive per sponsor); CNV-PLT-010 (two approvers, neither the author); SOC 1 ICFR expectations.
evidence: Supporting: model controlCheck (count rule, same-model [A]); OPS responsibility matrix (39 human elements). Challenging: CNV-GOV-003 text; OPS December sizing (9-15 FTE at 10k accounts); E04/E05 [M]. Admissibility: clauses are primary [S]; model and OPS are same-model inference.
assumptions: Explicit: a contracted reviewer counts toward separation; premium December hours are available. Shadow: the sponsor will appoint and pay for a third person; contractors may hold payment-chain access; auditors accept a 200-hour fractional reviewer as independent.
confidence: Low (that F3 is safe at go-live); Medium-High (narrow negative: F3 does not meet CNV-GOV-003 without a sponsor person).
owner_proposed: Owner (product owner) with the future controller; not accepted.
trigger: Signal: internal release-capable persons available per December day. Threshold: < 3 on any day with releases due. Trigger claim: three distinct persons are needed until the gate is accepted. Operational response: activate the pre-appointed sponsor releaser and surge retainer. Reassessment: move to F5/F6 before the second sponsor. Trigger reassessment: if the auditor accepts the deterministic gate, the threshold becomes 2 plus the gate.
go_conditions: Auditor SoD acceptance or a sponsor appointee roster; a December double-absence tabletop passed; reconciliation outside the payment chain.
failure_detection: Release suspensions > 0 per quarter; reconciliation breaks reviewed by the releaser; contractor share of payment-chain hours > 30%.
boundaries: No go-live with live money below three distinct release persons; no person releasing for >1 sponsor while SPD-ADV-001 stands.
commitment: Delay (F3 for live money); Commit to F5-with-reviewer as the go-live floor; Continue Experiment on the deterministic gate acceptance.
failure_pattern: Burden Externalization (Candidate): safety produced by sponsor appointees. Confidence Debt: 'minimum safe' asserted ahead of the auditor's view.
not_performed: Ownership acceptance; decision date; review cadence; outcome.
alternative_explanations: F3's lower break-even ($1.09B vs $1.12B operating) may reflect contractors priced at a 1.5x premium with no idle time, not a better organisation; at standalone F5 is lower ($1.39B vs $1.45B).
feedback_loops: Absence leads to suspended release, then backlog, then December overtime, then fatigue and more absence (reinforcing). A sponsor appointee covering release raises sponsor oversight cost and puts the renewal price under pressure.
dependencies: Sponsor board appointments; auditor SoD acceptance; contractor availability; the controller's dual role.
second_order: Contractors in the payment chain widen the access-control and background-check scope (SOC 1).
counterfactual: F5 with an independent reviewer at go-live costs ~$0.04M/yr more than F5 and removes the dependency on sponsor appointees for absence cover.

decision: Build investment level for the minimum servicing product: ~$1.0M (needs >=5x) vs ~$1.7-1.9M (1.5-2x) vs ~$2.4M (1x) plus safety floor
working_claim: The minimum safe servicing product costs $1.1-2.4M; agents make ~2x the planning case.
admissibility: Partially admissible: the range is bounded and conditional. It fails 'tidy-but-unearned models' where 2x is the base (no accepted-capability measurement; DEV). Restated: 'At base effort, 1x = $2.43M; any multiple above 1.5x is unmeasured; 5x+ is contradicted by Rehearsal 4.'
mechanism: Amdahl: ~30% of effort (decisions, review, integrations, accessibility/security verification) does not compress; agent compute is <5% of cost; bank/custodian certification and assurance are fixed.
signal: Measured human hours per accepted capability vs a blind conventional estimate (DEV protocol).
incentives: The owner's identity investment in Echelon favours high multiples; contractors and agents report completion optimistically (ordo: both agents' self-reported test results were wrong).
bounds: Greenfield, self-specified work only; regulated integrations unmeasured.
tradeoffs: A lower budget means more deferred scope (56% of the conventional scope), so labour moves to operations and sponsors (HC-12/13).
operational_test: Survives only if acceptance is independent; under time pressure the incompressible share rises (review is skipped first).
correctability: Moderately correctable if staged (capability by capability); low once committed to a single fixed-price contract
constraints: Safety floor before live money (pen test, SOC readiness, accessibility audit, bank/custodian certification); CNV-GOV-009 licence; second maintainer.
evidence: Supporting: Echelon output volume (internal-demonstration; 9,045 commits, 1 human). Challenging: Rehearsal 4 1/108 P0; no human-time data; $5M and $0.72M both unsupported (DEV). Proximity: none of the evidence is from a DAF build.
assumptions: Explicit: 132 person-months base effort; 70% compressible. Shadow: one human can review agent output at the required rate; the owner's time is free; tests written by the same agent are an adequate oracle.
confidence: Low (2x); Medium (that $1.0M is unsafe at <5x); Medium (1x = $2.4M at base effort, same-model decomposition).
owner_proposed: Owner (as technical lead) with an independent acceptance reviewer.
trigger: Signal: human hours per accepted capability / blind estimate. Threshold: > 0.67 on 2 of the first 3 capabilities (i.e. < 1.5x). Trigger claim: the multiple sets the budget. Response: re-base at 1x ($2.43M) and re-scope. Trigger reassessment: if capabilities differ widely in type, use per-type thresholds.
go_conditions: DEV measurement protocol in place (frozen acceptance, independent oracle, timer).
failure_detection: Defect escape > 1 high per 5 capabilities; rework > 20%; any financial-misstatement defect.
boundaries: Stage gates of <= $250k per capability group; no live money before the full mandatory set and safety floor.
commitment: Continue Experiment ($100-250k on 3-5 capabilities under the DEV protocol); Delay commitment to the full MSP budget.
failure_pattern: Confidence Debt (multiple assumed before measured); Burden Externalization (the owner's unpaid time).
alternative_explanations: High Echelon throughput may reflect greenfield, self-accepted, low-integration work rather than transferable productivity.
feedback_loops: Pressure to ship lowers review, which raises defect escape, which raises rework and maintenance (the effective multiple falls).
dependencies: The owner's time; independent acceptance; bank and custodian certification lead times.
second_order: Deferred scope returns as operating labour or retrofit (tenancy).
counterfactual: A contractor-built MSP at 1x ($2.43M) has known cost and none of the agent-measurement uncertainty, but costs $0.5-0.7M more than the 1.5-2x case.

decision: Entry sequence: A conventional / B product-first / C customer-funded / D narrow entry / E partnership / F founder-led / G hybrid
working_claim: Capital needed is $3.7-6M; founder-led F is cheapest ($3.75M) and customer-funded C is next ($5.19M).
admissibility: Fails false precision (capital to $10k from [A] timings) and hidden prescription (F's low capital relies on a $1.0B anchor signing at month 12 with no product and on F3 at go-live). Restated: 'On current assumptions the plans need $4.3-7.4M including omitted platform costs; F is lowest only if an anchor signs by month 12.'
mechanism: Capital = burn until fee cash covers fixed cost. Burn is set by build cost and time to first go-live; fee cash is set by sponsor size and collection lag.
signal: A signed LOI/contract with a minimum annual fee before the build passes ~$0.5M.
incentives: Design partners want low prices and custom scope (customisation x3 onboarding modifier); founders prefer narratives with low capital.
tradeoffs: F minimises capital but maximises key-person and control risk; D/G add revenue with commoditised demand; E halves margin (14 bps net).
operational_test: Sales cycles 2x: D and G never profitable within 60 months; F +$1.26M; partner withdrawal F +$3.39M, never profitable (failure-costs.csv).
correctability: Moderately correctable before the build commitment; low after
constraints: Licence (CNV-GOV-009); SOC 1 observation before the first staffed client; money-transmission opinion.
evidence: Model sequences [A] timings; COM: no public evidence of DAF design-partner prepayment. Same-model.
assumptions: Explicit: sign months, onboarding 6-12 months, $250k prepay. Shadow: buyers exist at 20 bps for $500M-1B books with $250k balances; no customisation; the founder can sell while building.
trigger: Signal: count of sponsors at proposal stage with a minimum fee. Threshold: 0 by month 9. Trigger claim: acquisition, not build, sets capital. Response: stop the build at the current gate; pivot to E or licensing. Trigger reassessment: if a partner commits funding, move the threshold to month 12.
go_conditions: LOI with minimum fee and data access for a shadow replay.
failure_detection: Cash at month 24 below -$4.5M (base B/C are -$4.0 to -4.2M).
boundaries: Capital committed in tranches tied to LOIs and capability gates.
commitment: Continue Experiment (customer discovery with a C/G structure); Delay the capital raise sizing until one LOI.
failure_pattern: Confidence Debt; Burden Externalization (design partner funds and tests the product).
alternative_explanations: F's low capital comes from one large anchor signing early, not from founder-led organisation design.
feedback_loops: A slow first sale extends the burn, which forces a smaller organisation, which weakens control evidence, which slows sales to regulated sponsors.
dependencies: An anchor or design partner; the licence; SOC observation timing.
second_order: A design partner's customisation becomes everyone's product (customisation modifier +$0.5-1.0M).
counterfactual: E (partnership) carries no money movement but never earns enough at 14 bps (year-5 profit $0.18M).

decision: Pricing structure: flat 20 bps vs per-account-led hybrid (~$350/acct + 3 bps, capped 20 bps) vs value share
working_claim: 20 bps is defensible only for some segments (COM).
admissibility: Admissible as bounded; the segment list is explicit. It fails only where 'value' figures are modelled, not observed.
mechanism: Buyer reservation price = best alternative (in-house 14-27 bps all-in for nationals, software 0.5-9 bps, BPO); servicer cost is per-account and per-event, not per-dollar.
incentives: Sponsor boards owe donors reasonable fees and will push savings through; incumbents re-tier selectively at renewal.
bounds: Small/mid-balance and already-outsourced books; high-balance books only via a per-account tariff.
tradeoffs: Per-account pricing protects margin on small accounts but may deter them; value share needs a measured baseline.
operational_test: Under incumbent re-tiering, flat 20 bps fails first; the per-account hybrid survives longer.
constraints: Payout-neutral billing; charitable-purpose safeguards on activity fees.
evidence: COM sponsor-value model (modelled) and observed price points (Ren/MS GIFT $737, USCGT $429, Stifel $1,142) [S, quality A-C].
assumptions: Shadow: the sponsor actually retires staff (value_high); balances are average billable, not year-end.
confidence: Medium (that flat 20 bps exceeds value at $1M+ balances); Low (that 20 bps is accepted anywhere by a new entrant).
trigger: Signal: price objections in the first 5-10 conversations. Threshold: more than half decline at the quoted per-account level. Trigger claim: the value model overstates avoided cost. Response: lower the per-account level or shift to value share. Trigger reassessment: if decliners cite risk rather than price, the signal measures trust, not price.
go_conditions: A tariff with a minimum annual fee in the first contract.
failure_detection: Realised fee < 15 bps book-weighted; minimum-fee top-ups > 20% of revenue.
boundaries: No discount below marginal cost plus the fixed-cost share at the contracted minimum.
failure_pattern: Confidence Debt (value modelled from 990 opex allocations).
alternative_explanations: Low switching may reflect migration risk and trust, not price.
feedback_loops: Per-account pricing discourages small accounts, raising balances and lowering the per-account burden; but it can conflict with sponsor donor-fee schedules.
dependencies: A measured baseline for value share; payout-neutral billing.
second_order: A price tied to sponsor savings invites audit rights and disputes.
counterfactual: Flat 20 bps on high-balance books exceeds equivalent-scope value in every COM base case.

decision: Reliance on Echelon: (a) runtime components in production, (b) development tooling and vendored UI/print only, (c) none
working_claim: Echelon lowers build and operating cost (research premise).
admissibility: Fails: no mechanism with evidence for cost reduction (DEV: credible saving $0-1.1M, conditional on measurement; LYR: Echelon makes Unbound $225k/yr more expensive at base). Restated: 'Echelon may lower construction cost of UI/print/schema tooling by $0-0.1M; any larger saving depends on unmeasured agent productivity; production reliance creates ~$0.27M/yr of new cost.'
mechanism: Reuse saves construction; reliance adds maintenance, security review, licence, second maintainer and upgrade churn.
signal: Executed commercial licence with escrow/fork right; second maintainer named.
incentives: The owner controls both sides, so the internal price is unconstrained. Investors in the servicer bear licence risk if ownership differs.
bounds: Tooling reuse yes; runtime reliance only with a licence and a second maintainer.
tradeoffs: (a) adds $0.27M/yr plus licence; (b) captures most of the build saving at low reliance cost; (c) forgoes $0-0.1M.
operational_test: Fails under pressure if the single maintainer is unavailable during an incident (bus factor 1).
correctability: Moderately correctable for tooling; low once runtime components are inside SOC scope
constraints: CNV-GOV-009; PolyForm-NC (charitable-organisation carve-out may not cover a commercial servicer); SOC 2 change management.
evidence: DEV [M] builds/tests of 26 repos; licence files; no production use; LYR layer costs [A].
assumptions: Shadow: Echelon's owner time is free; components remain maintained; the auditor accepts AI-authored components.
confidence: Medium-High (narrow negative: no runtime DAF capability exists in Echelon); Low (any operating-cost saving).
owner_proposed: Owner (conflict: owner on both sides; needs an independent director or adviser for the transfer price).
trigger: Signal: Echelon component in the servicer's production SBOM. Threshold: any, without an executed licence and a second maintainer. Trigger claim: production reliance creates fixed cost and a launch blocker. Response: vendor the code or replace it. Trigger reassessment: if Echelon gains a second commercial user, the costs are shared.
failure_detection: Upgrade hours > 10% of engineering time; open high-severity findings in Echelon components.
boundaries: Tooling-only reliance until licence and maintainer exist.
commitment: Commit to (b) tooling-only; Delay (a); Escalate the licence terms to counsel.
failure_pattern: Burden Externalization (shared resource treated as free); Governance Debt (related-party pricing).
not_performed: Ownership acceptance; independent transfer-pricing review; outcome.
alternative_explanations: The UI/print reuse benefit may come from the same owner reusing their own knowledge, which a second maintainer cannot inherit.
feedback_loops: Weekly 0.x releases mean upgrade work, then pinning, then drift from upstream, which erodes reuse value.
dependencies: Licence terms; a second maintainer; SOC 2 change management over components.
second_order: Related-party pricing between owner-controlled entities draws tax and investor scrutiny (26 U.S.C. 482 reading in LYR; not advice).
counterfactual: Tooling-only reuse keeps most of the build benefit and avoids ~$0.27M/yr of reliance cost.

subject: Observed Echelon development history (26 component repos)
system_context: Primary system: the owner's agent-assisted development practice. Context: Echelon portfolio, 2025-07-07 to 2026-11-25. Focus: why development cost per accepted capability cannot be stated.
outcome: 26 repos build; ~9,768 tests pass; 9,045 commits by 1 human identity plus agents over 105 commit days; no repo in production with external users; 0 of 1,687 Praxis execution records carry human time; 3 carry token counts (dev/report.jsonl, measured by DEV; not re-run by ADV2).
manifestations: No human-time field; no accepted DAF capability; 21 of 26 repos PolyForm-NC; no SAST or dependency scanning in any repo; Rehearsal 4 NOT ACCEPTED.
origin_network: Organizational: a single human builds, specifies and accepts the work. Technical: the telemetry schema records execution, not effort. Financial: no budget line attributes owner time. Regulatory: none yet (no regulated user).
propagation: Informational: output metrics (LOC, commits) substitute for cost metrics in downstream studies; the $5M and $60k/month figures propagated without derivation (DEV $5M trace).
evidence: Observation: git logs and test runs (DEV [M]). Inference: that throughput implies a productivity multiple (DEV labels it weak).
control_points: 1. A timer per work item with independent acceptance (high influence, high controllability, low cost). 2. A blind conventional estimate per capability (medium cost). 3. A second maintainer (high cost).
sufficiency: Sufficient: further diagnosis would not change the next action.
next_action: Instrument the next 3-5 Unbound capabilities with the DEV protocol before sizing D2.
claim_state: Development cost reduction: unsupported. Output volume: internal-demonstration.
unknowns: Owner hours; defect escape after acceptance; maintenance per capability.

subject: Rehearsal 4 autonomous build (indy-init-rehearsal-004)
system_context: Primary system: autonomous agent build run under the Echelon engineering system. Context: 420-minute rehearsal, 2026-10-27. Focus: why acceptance failed.
outcome: Independent verifier FAILED / NOT ACCEPTED; 1 PASS, 9 FAIL, 98 NOT_RUN of 108 P0 requirements; 296 of 420 minutes used (echelon-engineering-system/docs/rehearsal-evidence.md:13-31 @4ca2f98).
manifestations: Gates G5 and G8 failed; G1, G2, G4, G6 and G7 not run; D-HIST-WASM open; a token entered a failed Playwright trace and was rotated.
origin_network: Technical: CI-only WebAssembly diagnosis. Organizational: late integration of the acceptance format. These are the report author's interpretations, not observations.
propagation: Informational: unmapped P0-to-check evidence turned most requirements into NOT_RUN rather than FAIL.
evidence: Observation: verdict, ledger, clock (cited links; not read here, GitHub primary). Inference: the bottleneck causes. Secondary source quality B.
control_points: 1. Map every P0 to a check in the first hour. 2. Reproducible local WASM builds. Both are hypothesized by the source and undemonstrated.
ranking: Not defensible beyond the source's own ordering; confidence Low.
sufficiency: Sufficient for the next action relevant here: do not plan on >=5x autonomous construction. Not sufficient to estimate any multiple (not a DAF scope, n=1, token cost unmeasured).
next_action: Treat 5-10x as contradicted in D2. Require a comparable accepted run before using any autonomous-build multiple.
claim_state: 'Autonomous agents deliver an accepted product in one rehearsal': contradicted (n=1). 'Multiple >= 5x for DAF build': contradicted by analogy, not tested.
unknowns: Token cost; human intervention time; whether Rehearsal 5 would differ (NOT RUN).

subject: Ordo controlled agent-cost trial EX-SDE-2026-0001/0002
system_context: Primary system: a frozen feature mission in ordo. Focus: cost per mission and accuracy of agent self-reports.
outcome: 11 runs at $12.00-27.15 each; 5 verified; 6 void; both agents' self-reported test results were wrong (dev/report.jsonl).
manifestations: Void runs from telemetry/session restarts; incorrect self-reports.
origin_network: Technical: session restarts break telemetry. Human/organizational: the agent's self-report is used as an acceptance signal.
propagation: Informational: a wrong self-report would propagate to acceptance if no independent oracle existed.
evidence: Observation: run records (ordo/research/experiments/EX-SDE-2026-0001/0002). Not re-read in full by ADV2.
control_points: An independent oracle (already the DEV protocol's step 2).
sufficiency: Sufficient: compute is not the cost driver (<5%); human verification is.
claim_state: Compute cost per mission: internal-demonstration (one mission, one codebase).
